claim: Decode-phase layer gate localizes the second-token defect. The extended gate (decode re-arming on single-token forwards, mid-row positions-bypass for SGLang's context-threaded layer calls) compared both decode steps of the deterministic [27841, 3] run row-by-row against the NVIDIA decode4 golden. VERDICT: decode step 1 (row 2) layer 0 INPUT is bit-exact (rel_l2 0.0) while layer 0 OUTPUT diverges catastrophically (rel_l2 1.42, cos 0.37), and the divergence persists at rel_l2 ~1.0-1.9 through all 24 layers; row 3 (decode step 2) inherits it (1.4-2.2). Scaling analysis rules out zero/half/double state updates (best residual 0.94 at scale 0.5); corr(d_actual, d_expected)=0.57 means genuinely different state-dependent computation. Since layer 0 is a GDN layer whose decode-only code path is causal_conv1d_update (Triton) + the fused recurrent decode dispatcher (Triton) -- both bypassed entirely during prefill, which matched within noise -- the defect is pinned to the GDN decode kernel pair (or their state-slot indexing), NOT to m=1 GEMM precision (same GEMMs were exact in prefill) and NOT to the triton decode attention (full-attention layers 3/7/.. get already-corrupt inputs). The first token (from the 2-token prefill forward) is exact, which is why token 1 is correct and only token 2 diverges.
